A Court of Thorns and Roses #6

Regatul armoniei frânte

Sarah J. Maas, Andra Agafiței (Translator)

3.80
389,362 ratings59,247 reviews
Rate this book
Ce s-a frânt va fi creat din nou.

În inima continentului, Koschei Nemuritorul se trezește. A stat ferecat milenii la rând într-un lac de munte, dar acum amenințarea întoarcerii sale se răspândește pe nesimțite în ținuturile fae. În jurul lui se strâng aliați puternici, hotărâți să ia înapoi ce le-a aparținut odinioară: ținuturile muritorilor.

Regatul Nopții nu va sta deoparte cât timp nevinovații sunt atacați. Însă Prythianul abia începe să se refacă după războiul nimicitor cu Hybernul, iar unitatea pare tot mai greu de atins, cu fiecare zi.

Ca și cum n-ar fi de ajuns, cei care conduc și apără Regatul Nopții sunt încă zguduiți de trădări recente și de adevăruri ieșite la iveală, iar prăpăstiile dintre ei par de netrecut.

Ca să înfrângă umbra lui Koschei, care se întinde tot mai mult, vor trebui să se reapropie și să reînvie vechile alianțe. Iar ca să supraviețuiască, vor trebui să refacă armonia, acum frântă în jurul lor.

✩ Yaz ✩
732 reviews4,264 followers
February 25, 2021
His shadows had gathered around her feet, veritable dogs wagging their tails as if to say, We found her. Do we get a treat now?

The series needed to shift to multiple POVs, just look at how much the world has expanded.

A Court of Splintered Harmony was chaotic in a way I had not anticipated, but I am absolutely here for it. The title speaks for itself, the harmony was indeed splintered.

Coming off HOFAS, I expected us to dive straight into the crossover threads, but this is very much a set up book. The pacing and build-up make sense when you consider how much groundwork is being laid for these characters’ journeys and the overarching story that will unfold throughout the rest of the Cycle.

For Part One, it managed to cover a lot of ground while setting the stage for the next larger movements, and the wait till January will be absolute torture.



*** MAJOR SPOILERS AHEAD ***


✨ Feysand:

Rhys is in his “too old for this shit” era in this book, which makes it even funnier when you remember Azriel is actually older than Rhys.

The empathy Rhys extended Lucien really hit me deep. It just goes on to show you how excruciating his own pain must have been when Feyre was still with Tamlin. The fact that he can recognize the same suffering in someone he doesn’t really like that much just made me love him more for it.

Though, I didn’t like the fact that he wants to weaponize Lucien’s secret parentage to his own advantage. But that’s morally grey Rhys to you.

I love Rhys for standing on business and not accepting the High King BS. He understands the risks that come with ruling a much larger territory, and he is too attached to Velaris and the Night Court to leave it all behind.

We finally got some cute FeysandNyx moments!!

I love seeing Feysand living their domestic life and enjoy their little mundane moments, even with the world teetering on the brink of a war.

One of my favorite highlights of this book was Feyre and Nesta’s relationship. It was so healing for me to see these two sisters in particular open up to each other and easily talk. After everything they’ve been through, it really got me emotional.

Feyre is still grappling with playing the political game with these immortal Fae. And it’s realistic that she won’t always make the right call nor should we expect her to, it’s been what? 3 years since she turned Fae? and I liked seeing some tension between her and Rhys on the political front, they are still navigating that High Lord and High Lady dynamic between them. It adds another complex layer to their relationship.



✨ Nessian:

Nesta carried this book.
There is no doubt in my mind now who is the most
powerful character in the series.

The Inner Circle are right to be angry at Nesta for handing over the Mask to Bryce. That was a significant risk that could have jeopardized their whole world. But pushing her away was cruel. Especially from Cassian and Azriel’s end.

Her friendship was wonderful with Azriel in HOFAS, so reading about his resentment toward her really hurt.

I think it’s clear Nesta is set to take over the Prison and restore it to what it was. She is still finding her path in this world as she is yet to define who she is, a Valkyrie? A Night Court subject? Amren have been serving her some reality checks which I liked.

What hurt me the most is her fractured friendship with Gwyn. Gwyn was pivotal in Nesta’s healing journey in ACOSF, but we need to remember that Gwyn was willing to die with Nesta in the Blood Rite and Nesta went ahead and knocked her out. Gwyn felt betrayed.

I need my Valkyrie trio back and I know they will be back by ACOFM, and I cannot wait for them to have an even bigger presence in this Cycle more than they did in ACOSF.

As for Cassian, *sighs*.

I love Cassian, I call him Lord of sweethearts and I love Nessian. I’m not rooting for them to break up and it’s refreshing to see that even mated couples continue to face their own problems and challenges. A mating bond does not guarantee a happily ever after or have the mated couple live in eternal bliss and happiness.

I loved some of their moments in this book, but I am mad at Cassian for not bothering to check in on Nesta whose arm was shattered in her fight with Bryaxis. And then telling Rhys what Nesta shared with him in privacy was shitty, regardless of his intention. What I love about Nessian is Nesta is vulnerable and open with Cassian in a way she is not with anyone else. I think that trust between them is still fractured.

Eris is right, Cassian should be on his knees thanking the Mother everyday for having Nesta.



✨ Azriel:

I will preface by saying I love love LOVE Azriel.

I was not surprised in the least that his POV was messy, because I’d been anticipating it. It was clear since ACOMAF that Az was dealing with so much self-loath and it becomes more apparent with every installment. I’ve been saying for years that Azriel’s POV will be the darkest among the ACOTAR characters.

I absolutely loved the prelude and it set the foundation for understanding Azriel and where his issues stem from. That prelude is littered with details that will be very important for his healing journey and his mother’s words will echo true throughout his arc.

“You are an Illyrian, Azriel—the wind sings through your very blood. You cannot be caged. You cannot be broken. They lock you away because they fear you.”

She would kiss his brow once, twice. Because you are different. They could all feel it, from the moment you were born. And one day, you will show them why that is a wondrous thing.

Azriel spent the first 11 years of his life isolated from the real world, stripped of his Illyrian identity, and forced to witness the cruelty inflicted upon his mother. Since he was a child, the idea that he is an abomination, a monster, a demon was drilled into him. When those sentiments are instilled in a traumatized child, it becomes deeply woven into their identity, it’s not something they can easily discard, even centuries later as an adult.

He only had the shadows and the wind as companions. They were his only thread to the outside world.

Azriel is a tragic character in many ways. Deeply flawed and wounded. All of it shaped his perception of himself and why he is emotionally stunted.

Throughout the series, Azriel has displayed kindness and selflessness. There is so much goodness in him, even if he does not see it for himself.

The Azriel we are experiencing in this book, is someone who has reached rock bottom. He is on a path of self-destruction because the author needs him to reach that low point before he finds his way back up and embark on a healing journey.

Azriel’s journey is reminiscent of Aelin’s journey in Heir of Fire. Darker than Aelin’s, but similar in how it’s rooted in their self-loathing, their identity crisis, and their self-destructive tendencies.

Being in his head was whiplash after whiplash.

One moment, he is grieving the dreams he built around Mor and basking in her scent with a heavy heart, in the following chapter he is nuzzling Elain’s neck and calling her his salvation and he.. a soulless demon.

Azriel is a top-grade yearner. He is a romantic at heart. Much more than either Rhys and Cassian if I may be honest.

Which makes it much more tragic that he would seek affection to feel some sense of worthiness, but is not sure he would want that profound love he once longed for. He is very wounded. Azriel is not truly in love yet.

Azriel rarely thought Rhys or Feyre were fools, but to be that reckless, to be that in love— He’d never known such a feeling. Once, he’d longed for it with his entire being, but now . . . now he wasn’t sure if he ever wanted it.

Azriel’s relationship with the Mother is contradictory, because he mused about the possibility that the Mother have not given him a mate as she may find him unworthy thus validating his low perception of himself—but also he mockingly does not mind if the Mother condemns him if he pursued what he wanted (3 sisters + 3 brothers), It’s his way of challenging her for rejecting him and giving the third Archeron sister to Lucien instead of him—for daring to exclude him from that pattern.

With Mor, Azriel romanticized their shared suffering as a sign that they were destined. With Elain, he’s attached to 3 brothers + 3 sisters pattern. Azriel has the tendency to project his desires into the females he’s attached to and romanticizes what they represent to him.

And then we see that Azriel believes he found his salvation while the narrative keeps showing us a male who is self-destructing day by day.

Throughout his POV, more of his feelings come to surface. He doubts that true contentment would find him. He compares himself to Amarantha. It's very rare to make him smile. He deeply resents Truth-teller for abandoning him. He calls most of his dreams a fool’s dream. He wants to be rid of his shadows, wings, siphons and tattoos. He finds it hard to be careful when so much of his heart stopped caring. He was glad to see Illyrians piled dead around him during the Hybern War. He thinks the world should forget he existed. He places Elain on a purity pedestal to feed his own self-loath. He’a a monster, demon, an abomination. There is so much we got out of Azriel in this book. I devoured everything.

I do feel validated in the fact that I knew forbidden romance as a trope would be the worst trope to write for an Azriel romance, and the way he is unraveling is proof enough.

I will be leading the Azriel’s shadows protection squad and won’t tolerate any slander of them. They added a fun element to his own POV and the story overall.

While Azriel is linked to several plots, it is so clear to me that Illyria/Ramiel will be the most important plot for his arc.

✨ Azriel's Shadows:


I will say, I find it quite ironic that Azriel repeatedly expresses his desire to be rid of his Shadows, but when he is in danger or needs back-up, he seeks his those very shadows out.

Azriel has reached to a point where he despises everything about himself, including the shadows that protected him and remained by his side since childhood. The shadows that freed him and his mother.

For a character who is on a path of self-destruction and seeks to strip himself of everything that makes him who he is, that becoming the solution will not benefit his journey in any way.



✨Elain:

I really want to dive into her head and see what's there, because she did come off... suspicious in some ways in this book. Particularly in the way she hissed at Nesta and recoiled from the Made swords or how Azriel's shadows avoid her.

But other than that, I am glad we finally have a clear confirmation that Elain has been unhappy in the Night Court all these years. She is underutilized and dismissed. No one, not even Feyre, Nesta or Azriel saw how deeply unhappy she was. She was left attending and dealing with mundane tasks.

Although she expected Nesta or Feyre to coddle and not hold her accountable, I’m glad they gave her a reality check. Especially Nesta. But it’s clear as long as Elain is in the Night Court and among the Inner Circle, she will never grow as a character.

She's still grieving her humanity and Graysen, and I don’t blame her since she had the most to lose. She seems to resent her sisters for forgetting that they were ever human. She is yet to come to terms with being Fae.

She can easily articulate that she loved Graysen, but can’t express what she truly feels for Azriel. Her shutting him down as he was opening up about his childhood was further confirms the emotional intimacy between them is.. not really there.

They’re not on the same emotional wavelengths, what Elain might need from him is physical pleasure rather than emotional intimacy. They did not have one single meaningful conversation in the book. Everything was abrupt and happened off-page mostly. The lack of build-up is a glaring sign it's not meant to last. It serves as the catalyst for their own individual journeys and the fact it happened early on.

Furthermore, it's not misogynistic to expect Elain to at least have one conversation with Lucien about their bond. If Elain can learn about Fae customs and traditions to host their parties and festivities, it won't be hard to know how one rejects a bond, but she is actively avoiding making a choice on that.

She does not owe Lucien love or the bond, but it is a biological, soul bond that neither of them chose that is held in high regard. Wanting them to have a conversation about something that affects them BOTH does not mean she is forced to accept him. If you have both Rhys and Nesta calling her out for not rejecting the bond, that tells you enough. Yet somehow, wanting Elain to take a little bit of accountability turns half of the fandom and the characters into villains.

I did give Elain a round of applause by Chapter 24.

She is finally taking matters into her own hands and I have been anticipating for years whether she'll end up on the continent somehow.

I think it will be fun seeing her play the courtier and diplomat and we'll see how Elain shines in royal courts and ballrooms.

I don’t think any of the Inner Circle, including Azriel (who is forbidden from setting foot there anyway or he’ll jeopardize Mor’s mission), will chase her to Vallahan. SJM did not pull her out of Velaris only to have her in close proximity with people who were an obstacle to her growth.

Elain and Lucien’s relationship was stagnant for so long, Chapter 20 was needed to pull it out of that state and create some new conflict and tension between them.

They never interacted outside of the Night Court or away from the IC, it will be interesting to see how Elain and Lucien interact under new circumstances and new environments.



✨ Lucien:

The fact that Rhys did not kick Lucien out of the River House and allowed him to crash out and even almost k*ll Azriel, that tells you Rhys and the IC know and believe that Lucien had the right to be upset. He was humiliated and realized he is just a tool being used by them.

Since he showed up at the ceremony, he was nothing but respectful and courteous. Even during dinner while Az was trying to provoke him.

Spitting on Rhys and Feyre’s feet is not the most damning thing a character has done. Especially not in this series.

He went to Elain to apologize. His hand was shaking as he knocked the door. He KNOCKED. The reason he even came up to apologize was because Azriel mentioned Hybern.

What he had to witness was nothing short of cruel. And Rhys warned Azriel and Elain that they can hook up just not in his house and he does not want to be complicit in causing Lucien that excruciating pain.

Sure some of Lucien’s outbursts were influenced by the bond, but he held himself back and did not even blame or yell at Elain. He spoke to her twice: about the misunderstanding and him not darkening her doorstep again.

Anyone villainizing Lucien for this is contradicting the narrative, because it is clear the readers are meant to feel sympathy toward him.



✨ Gwyn:

Let me say it loud and clear: I support all her rights and all her wrongs.

Her first POV and I am down for her and ready to draw blood to defend her more than I ever did before.

I am so thrilled with how SJM is setting up Gwyn’s arc, and it might be darker than I anticipated but I am here for it and SJM excels in those type of arcs. Seeing readers who were previously indifferent to Gwyn now expressing their love and excitement for her genuinely makes me so happy, I've seen her potential since ACOSF and I know Gwyn will truly shine in this Cycle.

My girl is dealing with PTSD from the Rite and it is realistic for her to struggle with a moral dilemma—she trained as a Valkyrie based on their history, lore and training. No death was involved. It's one thing to wield a sword in training, and it’s another to stab it through real flesh and bone, to feel warm blood spilling down your arm.

For a character who was raped by a cruel male, who was surrounded by hateful males, I can see why taking back that power through violence might bring her a sense of temporary satisfaction and pleasure while scaring her at the same time. That moral dilemma is for her to navigate through and that makes her arc even more compelling.

Seeing some corners of the fandom villainize her is unsurprising to say the least, Azriel finding contentment and pleasure in seeing dead Illyrians around him is badass of him, but apparently we draw the line when a female character with a traumatic past experiences similar feelings. The hypocrisy is quite glaring to say the least but I trust SJM with this.



✨ Emerie:

Her blossoming friendship with Azriel has me so giddy!!

I am manifesting her POV in the next book, I’m so worried about what nightmare Bryaxis made her live through.

I knew that despite winning the Blood Rite and becoming the first Illyrian female to become Carynthian, it won’t mean much to the Illyrians. She had to return to her old life in Windhaven and conceal her achievements, lest they kick her out of the village. That is devastating to me.

Rhys even offered her the chance to draw Siphons and she rejected it.

Emerie will be pivotal in the Illyrian plot. In some ways, I can see her and Azriel becoming kindred spirits and understanding the suffering they were subjected to by the Illyrians—but also hope for something more and better for their own people. Especially the females

I think we will see her accept her title as Carynthian, we will see her draw her own siphons and use her Illyrian magic, and I am hopeful we see something blossom between her and Mor.



✨ Other Characters:

Mor: I didn't have much space for her, but I don't have much to say. Her slapping Azriel and calling him out on his fixation on unavailable females made me adore her more. I look forward to see more of her.

Clotho: I love her. I loved the new Priestesses lore it feels so rich. I do think there is more to her, but not in a nefarious way. One of my theories is Clotho is a Fate. Her defending Bryaxis was great.

Amren: I actually warmed up to Amren more in my last reread, and while I do think she’s being a little shady but I don’t expect her to turn into a villain. We might lose her in the future though.

Tarquin: he is so wise and I agree with every point he addressed regarding the upcoming war. He puts his court and his people first and that makes him a great High Lord.

Eris: I didn’t have it bad for him, but him in all of his silvery splendor and his silver rings and ornate warrior’s plate has me reconsidering. Hot damn I need fanart of this. I mean, what a man, he is still so down for Nesta.

Vassa: I’m finding her knowledge about Koscuhei a little bit sus. I think she knows more than she lets on.

Bryaxis: I love her. I don't care what anyone says. I think she has a sadder backstory and Clotho knows this. Manifesting her friendship with Gwyn.

So many characters have hit rock bottom, Azriel most of all, but I can't wait to see how each of them begin to ascend and find themselves.

The romances are going to be crucial because they are always part of a character’s growth and their healing journey. You know where I stand in terms of the ships.

I think Azriel will be involved with the Valkyries and will deal with the Illyrian and Prison plots (alongside other related plots), Nesta is definitely taking over the Prison, Elain and Mor will remain in the continent for a while and I think we will see Lucien there at some point. Feysand will commute to different Courts and Kingdoms.

I do wish we got a mention of the Red Star Rhys saw, who is actually Aelin, but Sarah might be saving that since I'm seeing more Throne of Glass threads being woven into the story.


I cannot wait for A Court of Forgotten Melody!!

Oh wow, Movement 1 was like being dunked in cold water and forced to meet with the ugliest parts of emotional torment you can imagine and yet something that you need to see and confront. I loved every messy moment of it. I've had some time to think about the events of this book. It's frustrating. Some of it made me scream, nearly throw the book at a wall, sob because it hurt too much but then there's this odd, lingering vulnerabilities to it that draws you in. I couldn't stop reading it. I loved how the mess was shown bitter enough to be labeled resentment, hatred, arrogance and agony. But there was so much love and desperation to be seen and chosen too, how does one overlook that?

Movement 1 definitely reads like it's being taken out of a bigger picture, which it is. And most of it won't land until we get the complete picture. But definitely read Crescent City before jumping into this. The narrative won't make sense without it.

I personally loved the political expansion here. That we're moving beyond the Night Court and Prythian. The continent had me curious for a long time now, and with how the chess pieces are moving on the board, I'm very intrigued by the direction this will take in ACOFM and I do have a theory for that which I'll expand on a bit later. The military and strategy developments are interesting but they need bit of an oopmh factor. It's a slow start to the movements but one worth reading, can't wait to see how it furthers the plot.

Loved to see Feysand as parents. Though the watery bowels have now turned into milky breasts. It's fine though, Feyre's nursing a six month year old baby. It's really not as annoying as people made it to be imo. But I loved seeing Rhysand's happiness being a father. No one deserves this more than the two of them. And oh my gods, Nyx, those baby scenes were so adorable.

I genuinely thought I could review this without spoilers but there is much to be dissected and I can't keep it all under the wraps with how much I need to scream. So stop here if you haven't read.

Also, apologies for the LONG review.

🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨

🚫 CONTAINS MAASSIVE SPOILERS 🚫

🌌 1. The Political Landscape: Night Court and it's Allies. Potential High King and Queen? 🌌

While I'm glad that we are moving on to a bigger scope of political warfare, something like ToG, there's a smudge of juvenile way of going about things. I don't mean it in a negative, it's just an observation. Sure, I loved seeing clashes of diplomacy play out and the new characters spewing their bs. But Feyre's vision however peaceful cannot be achieved by mere friendly relations. And both Rhysand and Eris see it for that. I loved how Eris paints the imagery of darkness being equally needed to balance the light. Sort of like Yin and Yang. And with Prythian itself not allying with that vision, it makes me see it as the courts need change and unity. Imo it was being set up for a High Queen rather a High King and I have just the right candidate in mind.

While Rhysand is loved and feared, he has adamantly refused to take up the mantle. And I genuinely think he doesn't want to. After 500+ years of ruling the Night Court, the wars and finally finding love and family, his arc has sort of reached a point where he would pass that wisdom to someone else. And we see that in ACOSH quite clearly. I don't see how anyone could misinterpret that. When he gives the troves back to Nesta, and her asking to be like him, that's clear as day. With Nesta being approached by Amren and eight pointed star, she's clearly being set for the High Queen/High Lady status. Narrative and pattern supports SJM putting women on a higher position and Nesta's story is not yet completed. It's a Valkyrie movement.

So will Prythian unify under a High Queen? Not instantly. But the tide may turn if a certain Autumn Heir takes his own mantle. Perhaps in the next book. I'm not going to elaborate on that yet, but there's been crumbs all over.

⚔️ 2. Nesta and Cassian: Reconciliation and Healing ⚔️

Good lord, this was painful to witness. I think the whole Nesta situation in regards to HOFAS is blown way out of proportion. She did not deserve that kind of isolation and judgement. That was not easy to witness. Especially from Cassian. And I guess the intent here was to show even mates have their marital issues or maybe Nesta needed to be on the journey alone. But I genuinely do not think that they're breaking up or Eris is going to swoop in and take Nesta. However hard the journey was here, reconciliation showed they love each other a lot. And I guess we also found out that perhaps you cannot un-mate. Cassian definitely needs to stand up more for her though, he had me a little frustrated and I still have to see effort from him. He is allowed to be upset, but the fact he even refused to hold her is genuinely baffling.

Nesta is a queen amongst women and love that Eris can see that. I don't mind a little healthy ribbing. And while we're talking about her. Hello??? The winnowing??? The chase against Bryaxis??? CHILLS.

🖤 3. Azriel: Trauma, Self Loathing and the difference between understanding and excusing him 🖤

I genuinely LOVE Azriel. I understand him completely. He's one of my favorite complex, morally grey characters written. And yet, with love, I'm still going to hold his character accountable. Trauma doesn't excuse the harm you cause. To self and to others. But while we're talking about Azriel, holy hell, the shadow lore we're getting. I loved finding out more about how his shadows operate. The inner mechanisms of his own mind and soul. It truly breaks my heart reading about his past and I sobbed so much especially the first few chapters. The way he sees himself, his wings and shadows, his siphons and his soul was downright devastating. He calls himself empty and yet all I saw was how deeply he's truly feeling. His struggles with Illyrian heritage is genuinely saddening to see. But from where he's coming from, I suppose it's valid.

I think the bit that hurt me the most was how desperate he is to get rid of his shadows. That he doesn't want to accept that one consistent part of him that's always seen him and yet he doesn't want it. And hence, that leads him to spiraling with the Elain thing. It's just one of the many triggers. The shadows behavior is worth watching, who they run from and who they feel happy around. And his reluctance to accept that part of him and the self loathing is making things worse.

Lmao tho I would admit his relationship and pettiness with Truth Teller had me cackling every time. I'm sorry I couldn't take it seriously at all.

I really hope to see his arrogant, cocky ass heal first before anything but I doubt it will be easy. He doesn't need humbling. He needs to feel seen and chosen. To be loved in the light rather than be someone's dirty secret. Nah, I love him. He doesn't deserve the hate for wanting to be chosen however wrong his methods to achieve that.

💙🩷 4. Elriel: A Ship Sinking 💙🩷

Oh, I'm going to risk the hate here. But I genuinely cannot see the love and romance here. Even if I pull away the mating bond with Lucien away for a few moments. Romantically? The book did not favor Elriel at all here. Everything, nearly everything happened off page. And let's remember, this is Movement 1. We're only going to move forward here. We won't go back to Elain's pov to revisit the romance that never happened. For a romantasy, taking out the biggest ship and not giving them the intimacy of emotions is not love. It reads like something brief and an infatuation that needed to be explored to be purged.

Their first kiss happens off page. We also don't see them connecting at all emotionally. There are no conversations between them when we actually see them connect. But what we do see is Azriel wanting to talk about his past to Elain and her pivoting the conversation to the bedroom. And however gentle she may have been, that shuts a door that Azriel was opening. That was written on page. We also see Elain consenting to be with him sexually. When Azriel asks if she's certain and she responds positively, there should have been no miscommunication. Sure, Elain can be confused but if you are, he deserves to know. She claims towards the end to Nesta that she saw a future with Azriel. And yet, it doesn't erase the fact that the moment Lucien caught them, the first thing she says is: It's a misunderstanding.

That does not support Elriel at all. In fact, I would go to say that the chemistry was wrong deliberately. Everything about it was written in a manner to make us feel the ick, the wrongness of them, the unease and how uncomfortable it's getting to see them like this.

Azriel is seeking light while being a secret affair in the dark to someone who could not listen to his past or his vulnerabilities. His shadows do not want a part of it, they see Lucien's pain rather than his own first. You cannot ask someone to be your light when the other person is keeping you in the dark. Fuck no. Azriel deserves better.

Not to forget that Azriel is also not clearly over Mor. At least not completely. He has conflicting emotions but he's not yet fully let go which I suspected as much. You don't get over a five century worth of pining in a manner of two years.

Coming to the fact, while Azriel may be advocating for Elain's autonomy, her body and choices, he also feels entitled to her. The three brothers and three sisters narrative from him was not sound. But I did see Rhysand holding them both accountable rightfully. No, Rhysand was not interfering. His argument was if you want Azriel, reject your fucking mate. It's simple as that. It's even more simpler that he doesn't want to be a complicit in the mess unfolding under his roof when he has a potential war to strategize. And it's understandable. He's a damn High Lord! His actions and support have consequences. So no, he wasn't stopping them. He just wanted no part of it.

The entitlement is to the point that Azriel feels the need to drag Lucien down the moment Lucien does something nice for the sisters during dinner. And yeah, no. That reeked of insecurity and desperation. He's not feeling secured with Elain at all. So how is it salvation? The imagery of life and death may be romantic but even Tamlin said to Feyre: I love you, thorns and all. Unfortunately, the evidence from Movement 1 is not in favor of Elriel.

Though I'm still a little curious if Movement 2 and 3 will address that necklace at all.

🦊 5. Lucien: A Deserving Male 🦊

I'm ngl the protective rage I felt could match the intensity of a mating bond. Cause what the fuck do you mean he had to endure another betrayal and humiliation by the hands of our beloved characters and no fucking one went to check on him??? I'm genuinely so sick and tired of everyone in the Night Court painting him as a "tool" to be used or as the enemy. We're six books in, and he's not smiled since Jesmida (in his own words). And we have not seen him sass or be playful since book 1. You would think that Azriel, who pined after Mor would understand Lucien and his scars the most but unfortunately no.

And it's not just the mating bond complexity that has me pissed which let's not forget, he didn't ask for either. No, it runs deeper. Because he has no home to go to. He has no friends but Jurian and Vassa. Feyre, who owes him better thinks of him as an "asset" or "tool." I'm utterly baffled by how Feyre has been treating him lately. He did leave everything behind to go with her.

Rhysand? Keeping the information about Helion from Lucien, not out of protectiveness but rather to use at the right time??? Yeah no.

And Azriel sending that repulsive spy after him? Cheap fucking shot. There was no need for this and I can see this backfiring.

✨ 6. Elain, Koschei and the Made weapon ✨

I mean, it's all very fascinating. I cannot wait to see where the story goes and what this other Made weapon is. But could it not be Elain? I'm just speculating. Given how everyone is coddling her, won't she have a reason to be bit of a morally grey reason to outwit others? Idk, I'm watching her closely especially since she left with Mor to Vallahan and Gwydion disappeared too. And with Azriel's shadows choosing to disappear around Elain and the timing of Bryaxis attack, I'm not truly convinced of Elain's innocence yet. She doesn't shy from telling Mor that looks and seduction can be a manipulative skill. I would personally raise red flags and alarm bells there. Her reaction during the confrontation with Nesta was very odd too, all the hissing and pushing back, I don't know what to make of it. Given how much she wants her humanity back, I'm not totally putting it off that she might be working with Koschei or at least under his influence. Again, not saying she's evil but she might be misguided.

But on another note, apart from Nesta, everyone coddles her so much, it's miserable on her end. She does try to open up conversations on helping around more than babysitting and gardening to Feyre, but gets shut down. It's not fair to her. So taking up space from everyone and going her own way? Approved. She needed that. This is perhaps the stepping stone in whatever she is to become.

Also another thought off the top of my head. Azriel trusts the winds and the shadows the most and yet we also notice how Koschei does have power over the winds and dreams. So how far, does the influence really go? Again, not saying Azriel is a villain here. But is he even listening to the right things? Are his shadows picking up on the actual truth??

Koschei's presence is described as death, no joy and without hope. Kind of like the mood of this book. Idk if it was intended to be this way or not. But interesting. Especially the contrast of death in Koschei and the life in baby Nyx. Could be nothing, could be something, I can't wait to find out.

💅 To conclude 💅

Things were messy here. Utterly chaotic and yet these were things that needed to happen. Without the explosions, no ship or romance would move forward. Without bringing a character down, there won't be a rise to their development arc. This is just Movement 1 and it started off with a banger. I can't wait to see where Movement 2 and 3 takes us. The action and political intrigue would be insane. Especially with Koschei coming out of his hellhole properly.

I'm so excited to see Elain's POV, along with Lucien's and Gwyn's. Gwyn is genuinely so precious to me, the potential there is amazing. She does not need Azriel but he definitely needs someone like her. The Valkyries are just starting and I'm here for it. I just know Azriel is going to have a tough time but the growth will be worth it. I'm not giving up on him at all. He deserves to be loved and he deserves his own healing arc. Here's hoping we get a desperate healing arc cause my baby is a little too destructive right now. I personally would love to see more of Eris. The potential is humongous and please for the love of the Cauldron, unravel the mystery with Mor.

The only reason this is 4.5 and not 5 stars for me is the fact that however much I loved and enjoyed this soap opera, I couldn't get behind how Lucien was treated. My blood boils like the flames of the Autumn Court. Other than that, I'm already waiting for ACOFM.

Review of advance copy
July 31, 2026
BUCKLE UP BITCHES 🗣‼️ i'm here to rant

I know that this story is split into 4 parts and scattered across three books. My rating for this book might change when the others are out, but for now, I am only judging it for what it is presented as.

SPOILERS OF COURSE !!! - (dont come crying in the comments later on)

Wow - we finally got another ACOTAR book 5 years later 😭 It honestly felt surreal to have it in my hands and read it. It was only 320 pages, but it did read like an ACOTAR book - in fact, it felt like reading ACOTAR all over again 🫣 I'm settling for a 3.25 for now because of how inconsistent I felt things were.

So, lets start.

The writing - idk why, but it felt so weird 😭 I was talking to my 10/10 absolute diva of a friend (some of you might know her as buket), and she told me that the writing was already bad 😭😭, and that we're just developing our frontal lobe now, so we're noticing - and I couldn't even disagree because some of the scenes (NOT ALL) were not well written, but the book was still enjoyable. I was hooked. It had me on it for ten hours straight, like I genuinely don't know what drugs were infused in it because I couldn't put it down despite the underwhelming writing. I binged it in a span of 12-13 hours. The plot saved the book. It was well handled, and the way it's moving makes it sound very promising, especially with how things ended.

I honestly think we're at this stage with SJM where we can criticize her writing if it's lacking 😭 because she's written multiple books, she has delivered time and time again, and if there is this lingering pattern creeping up where her writing is deteriorating (first HOFAS and now this), we can say it out loud. Some of the scenes were honestly so hard to read. The second-hand embarrassment I got from those scenes. The insane 'tell not show' thing going on, it felt more like a recap of the previous four books rather than a start of a new story (had me feeling a bit iffy at the start). I really miss the days when we would actually get characters on journeys in books. It added so much character depth, it would actually flesh them out, and make us root for them. It added a lot of value to the story but now there's zero importance regarding this and its barely in books. Especially here the characters are somehow transporting near the mortal lands, then to summer court, then back to the night court in like a span of a chapter 🙄

Also, i don't understand her fixation on some particular things, she would focus so much on such irrelevant stuff and bring it up at the most critical parts of the book 😡 (for example: Feyre breastfeeding or thinking about leaking milk 😭 rhys and feyre thinking about banging each other while talking abut alliance, Cassian and Nesta having argument and Cassian getting hard and wanting to bang.)

However, as the book progressed, I think I got more used to the writing because I started to enjoy the book and look past the problems that I had initially. I hate publishing restrictions because I would have loved to just read the entire thing in one go, and I think that would have encouraged me to give this book a higher rating because there are so many things that are clouding my thoughts right now, and only more answers can get it cleared up. I do believe that she ended this book at the right moment. The entire monologue between Nesta and Amren at the end felt so cinematic - that part was well written (credit where credit is due). I also think the next book is going to fare better since it has fewer problems to tackle. The wait time is three months instead of five years, so managed expectations and recent exposure to the characters and plot would make the experience better. The plot is also shaping up to be something grand, and I am excited to see where the Valkyrie cycle goes and if it's going to live up to its name.

I liked that the tension throughout the book was high, with Koschei the Deathless having this lingering dreadful feeling without even making a single appearance, the whole court drama, the human lands being at the risk of invasion, the Bryaxis jumpscare. It's safe to say it made this book not only eventful but easy to read through. It was atmospheric and tense, and you could, UNLIKE SOME CHARACTERS 😒, feel the urgency of the situation (ik ik, it feels conflicting when I praise it like that). Her prose might be subpar for the most part here, but her ability to write about high-stakes environments, creating an eerie atmosphere, is certainly not being put to question. Idk where she is going wrong with her prose or rather the execution of it because TOG had some of her best moments. Anyways, I love that we are moving forward in terms of the world as well, exploring new areas and more magical items - I'm a sucker for a book that gives its world building and magic system equal importance.

My ratings are more so based on what I've said above, but WE HAVE TO talk about the characters AND the romance.

We get multiple perspectives, with the most going to, I think, Azriel, then Feyre, then Nesta, then Cassian, and some small chapters for Lucien, Gwyn, and Mor (1-2 max).

Lets start with Azriel. From what I had read from ACOTAR to ACOSF, going into this book, my perception of Azriel was based on that, and we didn't know much of him. He's always been a mysterious character, so naturally, given the circumstances and how those books cater to his character through other characters' perspectives, is how you make your own thoughts and expectations of him. Being in Azriel's head was a totally different experience. I got whiplash going through it 😭 I loved the prologue. I think getting a perspective from his past was what I needed, and I wish we got to see more of him and his struggles alongside his mother. BUT I also do get that he has that part buried deep and isn't ready to talk it out, but knowing that part of his character gave us some answers and made his character more fleshed out. It also gave some reasoning to his actions - to an extent, and his behavior. Azriel might be caring, loving (to his family), protective, and aloof, but um 🫣 that's not all.

He's stubborn as hell, he's reckless, immature, entitled, impulsive, self-destructive. I think most of these emotions stem from his past and some from envy or jealousy of seeing his "brothers" have mates while he does not. I liked his perspective at the beginning because there was actually something happening 😭 but oh my god, after like 30%, his character read like a child throwing a tantrum. ITS CLEAR that this guy needs a massive healing arc - like he's in desperate need of it. I'm sorry, but you cannot be horny enough to be willing to risk such an important alliance, knowing that the threat this time is so much bigger. I always thought that he was going to be smart/clever and calculated, but boy, he was the opposite of that. He and Elain hooked up for a month, and out of those hookups, Rhys found out twice and had warned him a year before all this started. SO it's not even like this bitch didn't know the severity of the situation 😭 He was full-on lipsing with Elain in the kitchen, and when Rhysand appears and is like, mind you, very civil and logical, Azriel starts throwing tantrums and, mind you, f bombs. 😭 Rhysand says I have too much on my plate and I cant handle your shit. 500-year-old Azriel proceeds to say fUcK yOu. Never have I ever wanted to slap someone so fucking hard.

Then we get to the second scene before I start my rant for this (I was the biggest Azriel fan out there 😭 but the sheer aura loss that he suffered from in this scene was so heartbreaking and icky I cant). So Azriel is fondling Elain's boobies, and Lucien steps in - Azriel isn't warned because his shadows can't stand to be with him in the same room as Elain and they, like me (😝), are repulsed. He knows what he did is wrong, he knows that the woman that he did it with is humiliated, crying, and isn't even saying anything other than that this was a misunderstanding, and he knows her mate is there and what he is feeling. And keep this in mind: Rhysand told him his experience of WHAT HE FELT when he knew that Feyre was his mate and was with Tamlin, but still goaded him on and on - KNOWING that everything, every threat, is hanging on by a thread. ALL OF HIS FAMILY are there, and this bitch is there arguing with his fucking dick out 😭😭 like at least wear some damn pants because your shadows weren't covering you either CUZ THEY REFUSED TO LISTEN. He didn't think, he just did, and he ruined everything 😭 like literally Lucien, who could have helped them with Autumn and Spring Courts AND had Jurian and Vassa alongside him. The disdain and disappointment etched in everyone's face was so damn satisfying to see because he honestly deserved it, and he needed to be called out. When Mor slapped the shit out of him, it was so peaceful.

Feyre and Rhysand, oh my days 😭😭😭 Reading Feyre's perspective after 7ish years felt so damn weird. I enjoyed Feysand moments because they have their cute moments. I liked that beach scene a lot because I feel like it's important for relationships to have moments like that. I am also behind Rhysand on the High King thing because I DO NOT want him to be High King. We dont get Rhysand's perspective, so thankfully, we missed out on 400 mentions of my mate, but we did get a lot of Feyre's perspective. I was so scared that she was going to make Feyre only act as a mother and forget that she's super powerful and is also a High Lady, but I'm so glad that she did not do that because Feyre had that fire here, which I loved. However, some of the stuff that she did was super annoying 😭 Rhysand, I also liked. He was harsh, but he was super rational, and his decisions made sense 100%. Her, Rhys, and baby Nyx were soooo cute. I don't mind Feyre constantly mentioning breast leaking milk 😭 because she just gave birth to Nyx half a year ago, I think, and it would make sense for this to be mentioned, but it's done at the most weird times istg 😭 The smut scenes were so damn bad, like omg, I did not miss the smut chapters at all. The constant innuendo was so hard to read, and the sex scenes overall were an instant skim because I could not read borderline lactation kink pls 😭

Nesta and Cassian, GUYS 😭😭😭😭 I genuinely don't know how this happened BUT 😭😭😭 I LOVE NESTA?? Like, that's actually crazy. I was not fond of her at all. I think it's because she carried so much emotion in this book. She lowk carried the entire book on her back, so I will say thank you to her. I think I liked her so much more in this book because I agreed with her decision to give Bryce the mask. I know in the courts' eyes, it's a sign of betrayal, but it was the right choice. They knew it was the right choice, and they would have made the same choice if they had some time. Them being mad was justified, but them prolonging it was so damn stupid. Idewtt about Azriel rn because he NEEDS that desperate healing arc. Nesta did not deserve all the shit she got, especially from Cassian. Nesta single-handedly saved everyone's asses. Her scenes with Gwyn 😭 not this book living up to its name. I loved her and her bond with her sisters and her sisterhood. I loved how strong she was. Her single-handedly going against Bryaxis was so badass, and her drive to push against her abilities was so amazing to see. Also, Nesta clocking Elain at the end was so peaceful to see and was definitely needed, given how coddled she is. The next book will definitely have her as an integral part, given how it ended. Cassian is hard to hate, and I know that he's loyal to his High Lord, but some things are meant to be between you and your MATE. I think he should have the common sense to keep it that way, and also, him shutting her out for so long just pissed me off.

Amren and Mor, idc if I'm High Lord or Lady - if a 15000-year-old female comes up to me and says this wont work, and do this, I'll save my time and do that (no shade). Morrigan, the woman that you are. We got one slice of POV from her, and I ate it up. I cant wait for her book. I love her for slapping the shit out of Azriel and giving him shit because he DESERVED it. I'll be sending her prayers. Poor girl is stuck with Elain. I ALSO BETTER NOT HEAR ANY MOR IS EVIL allegations.

Gwyn, I'm super excited for where we are going with her character. There must be some importance to the highlight on the bonus chapter and her getting her own POV - I'm super excited. I don't think she's going to be evil as many think - Az calls himself a monster and a demon literally, so idt if Gwyn feels that, given how she has a traumatic past and how things are unraveling for her, is out of pocket. I think the second book's title also has to do something with her or the priestess in general. Idt SJM would use her in a villainous role, and also, isn't she based on her best friend?? Also she says she hates illyrian men but so does Az and cass 😭 and that she enjoyed killing those men in the rite but baby so did manon, lysandra, and aelin 😭 so let's not go there to justify her being a villain.

Lucien, I felt soooo bad for him, especially after I read his POV. This man has been nothing but kind and respectful, and I hate to see him being betrayed and broken like that.

Elain, omg, I hate her so much. She is the most useless character ever. I hate her with burning, raging passion, like I have not hated a character like her. She is so useless, like omg, and she says that don't coddle and don't infantilize me, and she gets herself in the worst position and then starts crying, like fucking crying. Bitch, what the fuck are you crying for?? Did you not think about the consequences at all?? Like, if she wants to sleep with Azriel, that's OKAY, she CAN, but like, have the decency to end things with your mate. Why is she stringing him around? I dOnT LiKe LuCiEn. I wAnT nOtHiNG tO dO WiTh HiM. Then break the damn bond and put both you and him out of that misery. She's actually so dumb, I can't, like she just pisses me off.

She says I can be useful and that she's a seer, but that stupid girl always talks in codes that by the time they figure things out, they would happen. I can see why no one asks her for help - also, she literally starts crying at every single thing. OMG, her victim complex is so strong, like she's also VERY much entitled and A RAGING PICK ME. Her going to Nesta and Feyre, apologizing for the plans she's destroyed because she knows they would forgive her, but when Nesta doesn't, she gets all defensive and starts backtracking, like bitch, weren't you here to apologize? ISTG SJM needs to do massive work on her character cuz I can't stand her character. ALSO, SHE'S A FUCKING SEER BUT HER DUMBASS IS CRYING 24/7 MAKING IT SO EASY FOR THE READERS TO FORGET THAT SHE HAS THINGS SHE CAN HELP WITH BUT OH NO ONE ASKS SO SHE WONT.

The romance, honestly 😭😭 this version of Azriel can stay the FUCK away from Gwyn. I don't think Elriel is endgame. If it is, I think there is a longggg way to go, LIKE a long way to go. Elain is in Vallahan, and I think her story will somehow tie up to Lucien's, while Azriel is in the House of Wind with Nesta. I think what's important here is that AZRIEL can get a proper arc and get his shit together and actually process his emotions and consider himself worthy of being loved because I'm sorry, their relationship felt super lusty. Not Azriel trying to open up, but Elain stops and says they should find a room to bang in, like hoe?? Is you fr?? Elain also needs to get her shit together. We need actual POV from her and to get inside her head and see what's going on so we can understand her. A majority of you havent read Tog and it shows 😭 sarah can easily switch up on who she wants as endgame. I do think with Azriel being in the House of Wind and his arc overlapping Gwyn's, I think that IN MY OPINION, there might be a high chance of that happening. Elucien 🫣 hopefully- idk, but hopefully.

Overall, I had fun ngl. It was messy and enjoyable.

Special mention to Areeba, Fiza and Hoda for going through this tough time with me
Special mention x2 for Shifu/Areeba for proof reading this review

Review of advance copy
March 19, 2021
Full Review (spoiler warning): 5/5

A Court of Splintered Harmony is the first part of one whole story, revealing some conflict and tension between political alliances and relationships throughout this movement.

There are forces at play regarding Koschei the Deathless, looming across the continent. With the way some characters were behaving in ACOSH, it leaves us wondering if Koschei is already pulling the strings within the Night Court. My heart ached for some of these characters throughout the book, but it's only the beginning of the story.

While Feyre and Rhysand and the rest of the IC seek to secure alliances and find out sensitive information, Elain is left on the back burner (for a reason), and we see her through the lenses of other pov's; her romance, particularly her relationships with Lucien Vanserra and Azriel the Shadowsinger, has then become a focal point in the overarching plot.

In ACOMAF, we learn Elain is mated to Lucien Vanserra right after being thrown into the cauldron and transforming into a Made Fae. Elain emerged as an entirely different being–without a choice in the changes in her body, the choice of a mate–with powers she has yet to fully master and utilize.

We also see young Azriel and how he became a shadowsinger, born from his trauma, and throughout ACOSH, his shadows disappear from Elain because she is the bright to his dark, the person who breathes life into him.

What particularly stood out to me was when members of the Inner Circle told Elain she can reject the mating bond while simultaneously telling her how important it is for Lucien to be an ally and asset to them. This would ultimately confuse Elain. How can she reject a bond to a person the Night Court may need for the impending war? Additionally, why would she reject the bond in a POV that is not hers?

For five books, Elain made it evidently clear she is not interested in Lucien Vanserra. As Elain said, "Lucien is nothing to me" in Chapter 22, ACOSH. I wish some acotar stans had more empathy for her choice and autonomy. We know that Elain cannot make that decision yet, with all the pressure going on around her.

I will admit we need Elain’s point of view to fully understand her thoughts and explore her feelings and visions for her life and future. But I cannot help but enjoy the beginning of the relationship between Elain and Azriel, and we know what Azriel thinks of her: “He was death, and she was life. Where his soul was soiled and bloodied, hers was pristine, verdant.”

Remember that ACOSH is part one, meaning the beginning of the story. Elain and Azriel have been friends since ACOMAF; it's about time they act on their feelings.

Furthermore, the Inner Circle and potentially darker forces are shown to keep Elain and Azriel apart. Their love is forbidden, with challenges from every corner that they will have to overcome in the upcoming movements. Those who think the Inner Circle being against their relationship is a sign they won’t end up together are simply not true.

The Inner Circle is against their relationship because their political alliances are already fragile. The IC does not speak on behalf of Elain, nor do they choose for her in her love life. That is the point of her story about choosing what she wants in the end, despite all odds against them. As Azriel said, “to hell with all of them, for trying to come between him and Elain, for not grasping what was so very obvious.” How do readers read the obvious and still dismiss it?

Some say Elain and Azriel have an unhealthy dynamic. I see it as two people who care about each other and act out on their feelings and need for each other. Their friendship began with ACOMAF, and their relationship began recently because Azriel was spooked about Nesta handing the mask to Bryce, which made him think, "This is my chance to express myself with her, as if the world was ending."

Do we also remember this is ACOTAR and not every relationship in this series began as sunshine and rainbows? It's amazing how people want to dismiss them entirely based on a three-hundred-page book (a tiny fraction of the whole story) when they have time to grow and develop in ACOFM (the much larger one). ACOFM will give us a better understanding of everyone's headspace.

Also, am I not the only one sensing something between Lucien and Vassa? He's very fond of and protective of her. I also believe Lucien will be the one to help break Vassa's curse, but we will see. I feel like many dislike Elain for their dynamic when he seems like he will be getting his own HEA after all; everyone just needs to be patient.

Additionally, I thought this book had some comedic undertones. There were moments when we were meant to be shocked. It felt like a telenovela; I think that's why I enjoyed it so much. Elain putting flower arrangements to block the view of her mate (comical!) The spy twins teasing Azriel (loved it!) Cassian finding out about Elain and Azriel (I nearly fell to the floor). The characters are meant to be flawed, messy, and misunderstood, which will leave the next arc to shed some light. It's called A Court of SPLINTERED Harmony.

The book ends with Elain wanting to do more than stand idly, and her journey to Vallahan to help stop Koschei will show all of her potential. For some reason, it felt like Elain was being forgotten, dismissed, and ignored; even her own sisters were forgetting her, too. Are the Inner Circle being influenced by Koschei? It all seemed very odd. Azriel’s last chapter ends with him wanting to find Elain to make things work, leaving their journey open-ended to continue in ACOFM.

Elain Archeron is the forgotten melody, and I cannot wait to read the rest of her story, her POV, along with the rest of the Inner Circle.

"His salvation–that was what Elain was, what he'd been willing to fight for"

...

For much of the duration of the series, Elain has been visibly uncomfortable around Lucien. She told Lucien that he had betrayed them. She had never shown interest in him, but it is evident she is interested in Azriel, which is mutual. That is a setup for the next book, which would be about her CHOICE.

Those who say Elain and Azriel's relationship would be obvious and cliché are missing the fact that two mated individuals (Elain and Lucien) getting together would also be obvious, cliché, and repetitive. Reading about choice and free will, choosing what you want instead of allowing "fate" to decide feels much more liberating to read. To say that Elain should be with Lucien because he is her mate is stripping her of the choice before she even gets to make it in her POV, so that argument is invalid.

Lucien told Elain they were mates right away, not giving her a choice, which was a mistake because, to Elain, choice matters. Usually, two people accept the bond normally when they are unaware of it; they become friends first and then lovers. Elucien is the only mating bond that had been known right away, which means it was doomed from the start because it makes them feel equally shackled.

Implying Elain and Azriel are only together now and would end up with other people does a disservice to their characters. Why would they use each other only to end up discovering their endgames are other people? You must think low of them. And why are they considered disgusting for acting on their mutual feelings? Why is Elain being called names when she's a newly fae who lost her old life, her old partner, everything she knew before, while her centuries-old mate whose had many years of life experiences get all the grace for his past mistakes and complicity in all those big changes in her life? Hmmm, I know the answer. It starts with an M. If you can understand and empathize with a man for his past mistakes as character development, Elain is owed the same grace.

Now, to those who think Elain is boring, her character has not been fully fleshed out yet for a reason (because it's reserved for her own POV). We will learn more about her, which is why we don't know much about her, but we know this: she's a seer, a flower-grower, a kingslayer, a hero of Prythian. That is by far impressive to me. I am more interested in getting to know Elain.

If you still think Elain's "boring" or "annoying," we don't know much about her. Some readers judge her before giving her a chance. Remember that Nesta was heavily hated prior to receiving her book; therefore, what makes you think Elain would not capture an audience? No one is asking you to read the books if you don't like Elain, so move on if that's not what YOU wanted. Mind you, the author gets to write what she wants to write; Elain haters do not dictate that at all.

Elain Archeron, you are so misunderstood

a book about fucking nothing. i was unaware it was possible to write this many pages about absolutely fucking nothing. and not nothing in the literary, contemplative sense. i mean NOTHING. no substantial plot, barely any character development, and an extraordinary commitment to making every conversation feel like we’re on the verge of something important happening and yet we never are. and what the fuck are they even planning? they sit around deliberating like the founding fathers drafting the declaration of independence😭✌️

azriel continues to benefit from the widespread misconception that being emotionally constipated constitutes a personality. you are NOT the guy pal, you are SO NOT the guy. rhys and feyre need to die already. preferably together, so we can finally explore what prythian looks like without the narrative constantly insisting that these two are the moral and intellectual pinnacle of civilisation. and elain, jesus fucking christ. can this wimpy child grow some balls? her perpetual helplessness would be considerably more interesting if the narrative actually interrogated it instead of treating her inability to stand up for herself as some admirable feminine virtue.

nesta carried, as always, but even her subplot was asscheeks boring. she’s one of the few characters with enough contradictions to sustain genuine psychological complexity, yet somehow even that potential gets buried beneath an astonishing amount of nothing.

and the prose. good fucking lord. sjm was never exactly a master of the written word to begin with, but this is particularly atrocious. every emotion is explained, repeated, rephrased and explained again in case the reader suffered a traumatic brain injury between paragraphs. there’s no subtlety, no trust in the audience, and very little distinction between genuine emotional depth and simply describing feelings at exhausting length. the characters aren’t allowed to be complicated so much as they’re allowed to repeatedly announce that they are. the book has so little to say about the characters it’s supposedly exploring. there is a difference between allowing a story to breathe and having absolutely no idea where it’s going.

an honourable mention to feyre’s breasts and breastfeeding, which i counted thirteen references to.

EDIT:
for the last fucking time, i read the author’s note. i know it’s one story divided into four parts. that doesn’t excuse 350 pages of virtually nothing happening until the last twenty. character-driven fiction still requires character development, foreshadowing isn’t a substitute for plot, and assigning profound meaning to every vague detail doesn’t magically make it subtle. i’m judging the book that exists, not the hypothetical masterpiece i’m expected to purchase in instalments.

and i’m not here to offer free editorial consultancy, or write some polite little review. i’m here to make people suffer. i want everyone begging for mercy, writhing in psychological agony, feeling thoroughly shat on, pissed on and set ablaze by the flames of hell itself.

if that offends your delicate sensibilities, you’re welcome to keep that information to yourself. if one more person mistakes criticising a commercially published novel as a personal attack on its author or everyone who enjoyed it, please go outside. touch some grass. touch some snow. hell, touch yourself while you’re at it. anything that might relieve the tension and restore some semblance of critical thinking.
