yikes, i am so sorry. this was an absolute and complete flop on my part. as always, this review is gonna be a hate review; take everything with a bucket of salt. i will be going through the whole book and there will be spoilers. major‼️SPOILERS‼️ in this review. i will be going into the details of why this didn't work. my opinion is just that—MY opinion. if you love this book, i am VERY happy for you. please do not come into my comments are talk shit because i am not in the mood. this will only be a review of the book, NOT the author/fans of the series. please read whatever you like. i am not the book police. <3

i’m going to just say one thing very clearly and that is that i understand this book is part of a much larger book and it should be read and understood as one story instead of as multiple parts to multiple books. even with all of that, this book is unbelievably chaotic and poorly written. taking aside the jarring character choices that SJM chose to portray—the narrative structure as a whole is extremely shallow and the characters are vapid and overly emotional in ways that make absolutely zero sense, regardless of whether or not you actually like these characters or these stories. we can honestly all agree that none of this is cohesive work of an author that has supposedly been writing for well over a decade. this feels like an entry-level story that somebody decided to write on wattpad after daydreaming about faeries. all overall TERRIBLE start to this supposed “new era”…so i’ll be going into full details of this mess.

let’s start with the obvious which is that this has unbelievably clunky writing. the prose is so substandard that it’s making me look like a literary scholar. now, SJM is not someone i particularly fuck with—however, this is a new low even for her. the dialogue in this book is so painfully contrived, it genuinely makes zero sense given the rest of the characters history not only with each other, but just in a world building standpoint. almost every single character is over 300 years old and yet if you told me that they are fucking three, i would definitely believe you. the unnecessary amount of temper tantrums that these people were throwing just because they didn’t get their way was giving me secondhand embarrassment to the maximum. some of her previous stylistic choices in writing is something that i have criticized in the past, however, it truly feels like this went through zero editorial processes, and this was a last ditch effort to make her fans happy seeing as none of it has anything to do with the previous work that she has put out.

before i get into the nitty-gritty in the specifics of why this book was absolute cow shit from somebody’s ass, i’m going to briefly talk about this fandom and their cult following hypocrisy when it comes to their favorite so-called “men”. you guys are absolutely fucking insane and it doesn’t surprise me in this slightest that everybody’s problem with this is that their favorite 500 year-old flop isn’t getting his happy ending. as i previously mentioned, i actually don’t care much for this author, even though i do hold a lot of these books close to me due to the mental health representation that it has. however, even with the little bit of leeway i can give her, it really doesn’t excuse this level of psychosis that the fandom has not only brought on themselves, but they push onto each other. i am very aware that SJM can only do so much and is not responsible for her readers, but it is very interesting to see how aware she is of her audience, and how she really tries to ignore what’s right in front of her. every time i’ve gotten on the internet, it’s only been about these men. it’s always: men, men, men. misogynistic ass people…

now that we are out of the basics, this is where i’m gonna go into full details of this terrible plot.

let’s start with everyone’s favorite topic of conversation—the politics. what the fuck was that? LMFAO? this was just horrendous. blunder after blunder. i believe SJM is a democrat, but this was full of right wing maga talking points. it was severely taking me out of the narrative. i’m gonna be completely transparent when i say i actually have no idea what this universe is about. what’s the end goal? why are they here? what’s their purpose? i don’t, and neither does she. the political intrigue in the world building is the most important part of any fantasy story. where is it? this is an absolute egregious failure on her behalf because this doesn’t stand strong due to the lack of anything happening. this entire book everybody is playing babysitter with each other and running around talking about some “close the walls”…pythian as a plot device is extremely under developed and has zero relevant to the bigger picture. it’s not some far away land where people come out to hide and are scheming against their enemies. its just a pretty little fantasy world where a bunch of these horny 500 year-old pigs are making it by thanks to the women and their efforts.

speaking of these circus clowns. jesus fucking christ. god save me please. the night court as an entity makes absolutely no goddamn sense. no logic whatsoever. i have no idea after almost 6 books, we are STILL expected to regard rhys as an exceptionally progressive leader when all he does is disregard his wife and his sisters in law. the absolute and utter buffoonery that occurred in a court of silver flames will never not fucking piss me off. the “pact” he had with feyre and his CHILD, it’s truly some of the worst writing and storytelling i’ve ever seen. i genuinely thought she would change this for her new book, but lord i was wrong. for a man who loves to emphasize the concept of choice and having the ability to make decision decisions for oneself, really disregard that when it’s convenient for him. a ruler is a ruler. sure. but, i wouldn’t have such high expectations if she wasn’t writing these characters in particular ways when it benefits her and her terrible choices. why go out of your way to emphasize rhys is more than just a ruler and cares about his family—when we have never seen this play out in action. this is a byproduct of not knowing what the fuck you’re talking about.

speaking of not knowing what you’re talking about, she is extremely hellbent on favoring the aesthetics and the lush environment over the plot. this COULD HAVE been an instagram post. that’s how little this matters in the long run. all of this genuinely could have been fit into the previous books bonus chapters, and nothing would have changed. no, that is not good storytelling and that is not building up to something bigger or better. this is laziness. having elaborate hierarchies and vast elements of self-declaration is not grounds for moving a plot forward. the entire inner circle is incredibly fucking toxic and are all operating on multiple levels lower than rhysand and his “wife”. the entire found family walks around eggshells when it comes to these people and can never voice their opinions, both personal or political without it turning into an entire fucking soap opera. i genuinely would not care in any other circumstances if this were truly the direction that we were going, however, SJM has made it very clear that she views the entire IC equal—emphasizing that they are family. at some point, we must be allowed to question whether these characters are genuinely competent leaders or are just the beneficiaries of a narrative that refuses to hold them to the standards it imposes onto everyone else.

speaking of these standards…gwyn, lucien, mor, amren, and hell, even elain. get the fuck out. these characters are absolutely shells of themselves and have nothing to do with this plot. as always, mr. high lord bitchass is the egregious one of the bunch and has everyone gripped by the balls. nobody can speak without it offending him, no one can just do what they want without him interfering, no one can have their main character moment without this fucker inserting himself. this is what we call favoritism. she is obviously extremely biased seeing as he is one of the first morally, gray fantasy men that garnered a huge amount of following from a primarily female audience. i get it, grandma. everybody wants to be like rhysand, but IT’S GETTING soporific. you’re so woke, you fell asleep. stop with the rhysand dick riding, it’s gotten so mundane. i’m genuinely extremely perplexed as to why she is so insistent on giving everyone their own stories and their own arcs when all she does is revert back to rhys and co. even feyre—the actual main protagonist—doesn’t get glazed this much. if she was this obsessed with rhys, she could’ve just given him another book. why make it clear that “everyone wil have their story told” and then obviously favor certain characters over others. azriel and elain are the remaining two “main characters” with no development or storyline.

speaking of azriel and elain…girl. what the hell was that? i am probably in the minority when i say—they make the most sense ship wise. it was clearly building up to this being endgame but the way it was executed was so cheap. so so shoddy. i’m actually losing my mind because of how horribly all of that played out. even after they “hooked up” a few times, it makes sense that they will be endgame because of HOW he spoke about her. the whole point of this relationship was a slowburn. it was building up since mist and fury with an obvious forbidden aspect since elain and lucien are mated, and daddy rhysand barred them from seeing one another. so color me surprised when i say, nothing happened. no build up, no slowburn, no tension, no angst, no chemistry, no nothing. this was the most nothingburger relationship ever. they had so many moments in the previous books where their outside nature could have truly shined, but instead—we were more focused on the bullshit and did not let any of that come through with the plot. these two are ghosts of the people they used to be. the only element of this book that makes sense is how possessive azriel is of elain and how he wants everything in his control. his deportment there makes sense. 100%. but baiting lucien? throwing toddler tantrums with rhys? being so loud and obnoxious? having manic episodes with this so called family? GIRL. you have 500 fucking years of age that you possess. THE most embarrassing part of this is when they all walked in on elain & azriel NAKED…and then both just stood there and did nothing. i’m fucking screaming LMFAO. SJM must think we are a group of jokers because in what world is this romantic? i was dying of embarrassment at how inadequately everything was playing out. azriel is easily the smartest character in this universe but lord have mercy. love does make you blind because get out with the tomfoolery.

now, don’t get this twisted into thinking i’m here for the utter tomfoolery that is gywnriel and elucien. fuck these flop ass relationships, because i don’t care. gywn is a good side character to nesta’s story but she does NOT need a man to be interesting. azriel doesn’t even like or see her that way, and she couldn’t give less of a fuck if she tried. i find it hilarious how these fans self-insert with her because they want to pretend they are with azriel. the same goes for lucien’s grandpa ass. bro is too old for a bunch of middle-aged women to be crying over him being lonely. nobody gives a fuck. elain owes him nothing and it’s getting very creepy how women who are reading romantasy of all things are forcing this bond and coming for elain for not wanting him. all this poor baby talk has me gagging. he’ll be fine. he’s deadass centuries old who is also a boring cunt but…that’s neither here nor there. the whole point of this story is CHOICE. elain gets to choose. azriel gets to CHOOSE. they are the two most dismissed characters where every time they try to speak or voice their opinions, they get shut down and told to mind their business. i’m irritated with everyone getting their point of view. we don’t care. please stick to ONE story. this isn’t game of thrones.

i’m always heavily intrigued by the silent girl in fantasy books that always gets spoken for, but it seems like SJM doesn’t even know what she wants to do with her because how are we almost 6 books into the series and she doesn’t even have one goddamn thought to herself??? it’s actually irritating to see how feysand & nessian had their story. they had their romance, their arcs, their points of view. elriel? ZILCH. people already hold women in romance storylines at a much higher standard than they ever would a man—and this is not helping all of the delusional women out there that self-insert with their favorite bat boys. the structure was always there. 3 brothers with 3 sisters. it was the perfect set up. they both are each other's mirrors. like calls to like. azriel is the quiet damaged loner. elain is the dismissed, forgotten middle sister. azriel is very clearly in love and obsessed…elain wants someone who sees and treats her as equal. they both HAVE something. this isn’t built off a fanfiction fantasy like the other couples. they’ve had as much time to develop with nesta and cassian. both of these relationships started around the same time. everything was laying out crystal clear…but of course, i should’ve known this would flop because this fandom has no idea what they're talking about. people are way too quick to force azriel in relationships with everyone and their mother just BECAUSE they hate elain. people don't ship lucien + elain because they love them together. it's because they feel bad for that man. people don't ship gywn + azriel because they have this soul shattering chemistry and connection. it's because they HATE elain. if 2+ 2 = 4...this level of delusion is actually crazy.

overall, if you like this book, that is literally your prerogative. if you’re gonna come for me for reading this because this is obviously a negative review, please pack it all the way up. i first picked up these books when i was severely depressed, and due to that it holds a special place in my heart whether i want it to or not. i had this entire book and storyline leaked to me at the very end of august, so ultimately, i made the decision to just read it to get the full picture and because once upon a time ago—i was heavily invested in these characters. i’ll definitely read the next part of this very long book just to get the most accurate depiction of the story that she was desperately trying to portray. but no. i’m not giving this a very low rating because it is the beginning portion of a much larger plot. books can be “well written” even with 100 pages. this is just not one of them and i of all people, am not surprised by this because this is a clear indication of a last-ditch attempt to write something after multiple years of leaving your very, very large audience with nothing. she is also very clearly milking this for everything that she can because the love triangle debacle should’ve been shut down way back when…and let’s be honest here—she easily could’ve fit everything into two books but how else will capitalism work? i refuse to believe this is the work of a highly established fantasy author.

this reads like a fucking prequel novella written by eric kripke. i’m so done.

a court of manas lost her fucking braincells.

Review of advance copy
February 13, 2021
So I get the whole point of this particular story/title is that allies and people are splintering the harmony they'd previously had to set up the next two books...but one issue I have with this author in particular (and I say this as a lifelong fan of her work) is that sometimes she'll write characters that to ME seem OOC to further the plot. Instead of writing what narratively fits that character, she'll have the character act the way she wants to in that moment regardless of if it makes sense or not. Idk if I'm wording this well, but hopefully you get what I mean.

ALMOST. EVERY. SINGLE. CHARACTER. LOST. ALL. THEIR. GROWTH. Minus maybe Feyre?

I also didn't like how many POV's this one had...it felt unnecessary.

Now onto my biggest issue with this book....SJM has talked for years now about writing and planning for Elain's book, yes, BOOK, implying she would get her own. Only to make her share her story with like ten other POVs? She has SO much story to tell, we know next to nothing about her or her seer powers, if she has any others? Why does the cauldron favor her so much? Will she break the mating bond? Will a blood duel happen? Will she follow where her heart seems to be leading even if it's forbidden? I had such high expectations for this one and the only time we really see Elain get a chance to speak up is through Mor at the very end. Like, with Mor? Really? You couldn't make that last POV Elain to set up her story?

It just really felt like Elain is the punching bag of this fandom and author, who repeatedly made her out to be the bad guy in this book when it was NOT necessary while at the same time pandering to the boy moms of the fandom by giving Lucien and Azriel POV's to make them more sympathetic than the girl in the triangle....

I truly understand that an Elain POV is 100% probably happening in the next book, but is it really even going to be satisfying when she's sharing her story with everyone else? How much focus will she really be able to get with so much going on? I don't understand why we couldn't have made this next book all Elain and then the final one multiple POV to wrap things up? I digress.

I STILL don't care about Nesta and Cassian as a couple and maybe SJM isn't done with their story but I was just bored with their repeated problems and they still don't seem like a good fit to me. Also controversial opinion since I know so many love Nesta, but I just don't care to have more of her POV at this time, we JUST had a huge book of her and she's still getting this much focus? I don't mind her playing a part as a side, but again, can we move onto something new?

I did enjoy seeing Feyre as a mom and how she didn't lose her ambition and worth and focus as a character just because she suddenly became a mom, that was probably the highlight of the book to me. I had missed being in her head and to see a leading lady being a mom in a romantasy series is something we almost NEVER see or touch upon, I found all that very touching.



Idk, I just feel let down with the direction of this series going forward and I worry that her best writing may be behind her. I hope SJM proves me wrong.

ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ⋅ ☾ There is a single excuse for everything that happened in this book, and that is only if Koschei has somehow managed to infiltrate these people's minds and start influencing them. ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ⋅ ☾ Don't even ask me who my favourite character in this book was, because I can already tell you it was the shadows. Yes, Azriel's shadows. At this point, they deserve their own character arc, a dedicated fanbase, and probably more appreciation than half the actual cast.

ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ⋅ ☾ Feyre's leaking breasts are the new watery bowels????? ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ What exactly is Feyre's problem??? Did motherhood suddenly make her unbearable? ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ And I see these two still need to remind us every few pages that he is "her mate" and she is his "Feyre darling". WE GET IT. STOP!!!!!

ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ⋅ ☾ Speaking of characters who desperately need to get their shit together, shall we begin? AZRIEL DOESN'T NEED SEX. ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ I am sorry, but I never understood the hype surrounding him in the first place, and this book only convinced me further that he needs urgent help. ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ He might be a very complex character, and he might have a very amazing character arc in the future, but for now? He is my number one enemy. ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ There was no reason for Azriel to act the way he did towards Lucien, and he was behaving like the biggest, pettiest manchild ever. Or maybe he just wants a piece of the redhead for himself; after all, he was constantly noticing how beautiful, handsome, and pretty Lucien was, right?

ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ⋅ ☾ I am saying this as someone who really doesn't give a shit about this entire ship war and couldn't care less about who Azriel ends up with (hopefully with a therapist): there is no fucking way anyone read this book and thought even for one goddamn moment that what was happening between Az and Elain was romantic. ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ His shadows think they are me for the way they avoid Elain like the plague; each time he is around her, he feels like he is losing parts of himself (which he, in his idiocy, takes as a good sign), she doesn't give a shit about him emotionally and she only wants to fuck him.
